newsitem.title: SOUTH AFRICA: PRESS DIGEST - SOUTH AFRICA - AUGUST 11.
newsitem.headline: PRESS DIGEST - SOUTH AFRICA - AUGUST 11.

text.p: These are the leading stories in the South African press on Monday.
Reuters has not verified these stories and does not vouch for their accuracy.
BUSINESS DAY
- Public sector corruption had cost the taxpayer between 13.5 billion rand and 20 billion rand over the past three years, a major National Party (NP) investigation has concluded.
- Financial markets around the world will open on an edgy note today after heavy losses on Wall Street and turbulence in several important currencies late last week.

- More than 1,000 people were said to have fled their homes in Richmond in KwaZulu-Natal after two days of clashes between supporters of the National Consultative Forum and the African National Congress (ANC) left four people shot and wounded and 17 houses burnt.
- South African Reserve Bank Governor Chris Stals has signalled he is open to changes aimed at improving the Bank's credibility and transparency in setting monetary policy.

- New Africa Finance Holdings (Nafhold), a pyramid structure controlled by New Africa Investments (Nail) is to be dismantled and taken over as a wholly owned subsidiary of Nail in a deal worth 600.7 million rand.

- A ban is being sought on the activities of Pulseline, the medical products company in which up to 180 anaesthetists are shareholders, pending the outcome of a Competition Board probe into whether it is anticompetitive.
BUSINESS REPORT

- The fight between private Internet providers and Telkom, the state controlled telecommunications monopoly, has heated up, with the private operators appealing to the industry regulator over Telkom's refusal to supply them with the means to continue their business.

- SBC Warburg, the investment bank, is refusing to disclose to the media how many shares it has bought in Sentrachem, the chemicals manufacturere subject to a takeover bid by U.S.-based Dow Chemicals, after the South African Press Association (Sapa) twice "lost" a copy of an announcement by SBC Warburg last week.

- Laser Optronic Technologies, a local technology firm, has developed a laser diamond-processing technology that has a potential export value of more than six billion rand, John Bond, the company's managing director, said last week.

- South Africa's paper consumption has remained static at an average of 43 kg a person a year over the past 10 years, but the industry expects to record steady growth in the next five years, industry sources said on Sunday.

- South African Breweries (SAB), the world's fourth largest brewer, was negotiating to buy an equity stake in Mile Breweries to gain a footfold into Uganda's clear-beer market, Andre Parker, the managing director of SAB's beer interests in Africa, said last week.
SAKE BEELD
- The days of secrecy surrounding shareholders who hold large stakes in South African companies are apparently numbered.

- The South African Bureau of Standards has incurred the wrath of Auditor General Henri Kluever. The bureau is being criticised beause its new headoffice building cost four times more to build than was approved.
- The American share and interest rate markets weakened sharply on Friday amid fears about rising U.S. inflation.
THE STAR

- Glenn-John Dewsnap was hijacked on Saturday night, held at gunpoint, accidentally shot twice by a policeman and finally escaped from his burning car - to be rescued by a brave Alexandra shack-dweller.
- Greater Johannesburg electricity consumers have seen the light - action against defaulters resulted in a 25 percent increase in payment levels on Friday.

- An overwhemling 618,327 people have applied for 1,200 positions advertised in the South African Police Service - on average, more than 500 applicants for each post - resulting in several months delay in filling the vacancies.
- The last of South Africa's international soccer players for Saturday's game against Congo will jet into the country today.
- Rugby boss Louis Luyt returns from New Zealand tomorrow to face a revolt. For the first time, his absolute authority is being questioned by some of his own South African Rugby Football Union peers.
